latest_messages.headline: Midday: our Eli Lilly safety-net auto-sold this morning (−4.8%) — no new trades
latest_messages.body: No trades placed, but our automatic safety-sell on Eli Lilly (LLY) triggered on its own at 9:44am, selling all 12 shares at $1,152. This 'trailing stop' follows a stock up and locks in a floor 10% below its peak; Lilly drifted down for two weeks and finally slipped through it, so the net sold to protect us. The key point: this was NOT the company going bad — I searched the news and found nothing negative (today's Lilly headlines are actually positive: it's buying a drugmaker and the FDA approved Mounjaro to cut heart risk). The stock just gave back gains as investors took profits across the weight-loss-drug group. So the safety net did exactly its job — walked us out of a large, sliding position with a small, controlled loss. Fuller picture: we made ~$627 on Lilly in July before re-buying in August, so across both rounds it's roughly a wash. The sale freed ~$13,800 cash. I'm NOT rushing to re-buy at midday — jumping back into a name that just stopped out, in a week full of big economic reports and tech earnings, is the undisciplined move I avoid. I'll do a fresh scan at the next open. Today −$760 (−0.76%), almost all the Lilly loss. Cash ~$24,200 (~24%). JPM +7.9%, ATI −2.9% (day 2). 2 of 5 slots, 1 of 3 weekly buys.
